parts.text: Which claim correctly decides that a sample is a mixture?

options.text: Salt-water is a mixture because salt and water are physically mixed and each keeps its own properties.
Oil-on-water is not a mixture because both materials are liquids.
Salt-water is not a mixture because the salt can no longer be seen separately.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Preeti stirs salt into water until the salt dissolves. She can still taste the salt, and the water still feels wet. Separately, she pours oil onto water; the oil floats as a layer that stays visible.

part_answers.answer: A mixture has two or more substances physically mixed while each keeps its own properties; salt-water shows that.

teacher.key_rationale: A mixture has two or more substances physically mixed with each keeping its properties. Salt-water fits. Being unseen or both liquids does not decide otherwise.
